title: Trace validation and normalization adapter with per-tenant exporter routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: introduce a lightweight Trace Validation & Normalization Adapter (TVNA) that runs as a pre-export processor in the OTEL pipeline. Goals: (1) ensure incoming spans conform to Redwood canonical span schema; (2) remap common legacy vendor tags to canonical attributes; (3) enforce tenant-id propagation and early rejection for malformed/unsigned spans; (4) compute and set synthetic service.name and environment fields when missing; (5) provide a pluggable outbound routing layer to send spans to Tempo, Jaeger, or an archival sink per tenant; (6) perform adaptive batching to avoid downstream payload rejections.

Scope: TVNA will sit between our OTLP ingest and existing exporter dispatcher. It will be implemented as a Go service packaged as a filter in our existing span-relay binary (configurable feature flag). Implementation includes a normalization rule engine (YAML-driven), validation metrics, exporter adapters for Tempo (HTTP proto with dynamic routes), Jaeger (Thrift/GRPC as needed), and an S3-compatible archival adapter for long-term storage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Incoming spans failing schema validation increment validation_fail_rate and are dropped with generated reason codes in logs.
- Normalization rules support search/replace and conditional mapping (e.g., map "http.status" -> "http.status_code"; remap legacy tag "host" -> "host.name").
- Per-tenant routing config allows mapping tenant -> [primary_exporter, fallback_exporter], with weights and max_batch_bytes.
- Exporter adapters expose exporter_latency_ms and exporter_retries metrics and respect per-tenant credentials.
- End-to-end integration test that verifies remapping, tenant routing, and adaptive batching behavior under synthetic high-throughput load.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- We choose validation at the ingest edge to fail fast and reduce downstream noise; downside is the added CPU at the edge. Mitigation: lightweight checks first (presence of tenant, traceid validity) and expensive checks optional behind feature flags.
- Normalization is rule-driven rather than hard-coded to allow iterative updates; risk is rule combinatorics causing accidental overwrites — rules have explicit priority and audit logging.
- Adaptive batching aims to keep downstream payloads under configured size; this will slightly increase latency for large bursts. We'll tune max_batch_bytes per exporter to preserve Tempo's ingestion constraints.

Telemetry/key metrics introduced:
- validation_fail_rate (counter)
- validation_reject_reasons (counter, label by reason)
- normalization_rewrites (counter)
- tenant_exporter_route_changes (counter)
- exporter_batch_size_bytes (histogram)
- exporter_latency_ms (histogram)

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gate: default off for all tenants. Unit/integration tests green.
2) Internal canary: enable for Redwood internal tenant traffic + dev staging tenants for 48h; monitor validation_fail_rate and exporter_latency_ms.
3) Select low-volume customer tenants (5) with opt-in flag for 72h.
4) Gradual ramp with automated rollback if validation_fail_rate > 0.5% or exporter_latency_ms P95 increases by >20%.
5) Open to all tenants with migration assistance and runbook.

Operational runbook (short):
- If validation_fail_rate spikes: switch feature flag to off, inspect last 10000 rejected spans via temporary debug dump at /debug/recent-invalid (auth required).
- If exporter_retries spike: check credential rotation log and per-tenant route config; fallback to archival sink to avoid data loss.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: legitimate spans rejected due to aggressive rules. Mitigation: soft-reject mode that tags spans and sends to a dead-letter archive for inspection before hard blocking.
- Risk: added CPU on ingest nodes. Mitigation: enable sampling, offload heavy normalization to a dedicated worker pool.

Notes on compliance: adapter will mark 'redwood.processed_by' attribute and record a per-tenant audit log entry for any rewriting that changes PII-like attributes. KMS keys used for exporter credentials must be loaded per-config and never logged.
